name: Kandinsky / Synesthetic Abstraction
summary: Fine-art canvas UI after Kandinsky: warm cream ground, overlapping circles, quarter-arcs, and ruled line-segments in red/yellow/blue struck with 3px black outlines, arranged like a musical score and moving only in slow, contemplative drift.
whenToUse: When the user asks for Kandinsky, Bauhaus or Russian-avant-garde geometry, an abstract-composition look, circles-and-arcs motifs, a museum or gallery art direction, "color as sound" synesthesia, or a calm fine-art canvas interface instead of a retro screen.
rules: Compose, don't decorate: arrange circles, quarter-arcs, triangles, and line-segments on an invisible 8px grid the way a score places notes — pick one dominant mass, one counterweight, and one line that travels between them, then stop before the canvas fills up.

Outline everything: every circle, arc, triangle, and rule carries a 3px #111111 stroke, and fills come only from the trio — red #d62828, blue #1d4ed8, yellow #f4b400 — plus cream #f7f2e8, paper #fdfaf3, and white #fafafa for the ground.
Keep the ground warm and quiet: page is #f7f2e8, cards lift to #fdfaf3, and no hue outside the trio appears as a fill; a violet or teal gradient instantly reads as a modern app instead of a painting.
Radius stays 0 on every rectangle — a panel is a ruled rectangle, and the only curves in the system are whole circles and arcs drawn as motifs, so rounding a card to 12px fights the geometry.
Depth is a stamped ink offset, 3px 3px 0 #111111, and nothing more; the single allowed soft lift is 0 16px 40px rgba(17,17,17,.08) for a floating plate, plus a 3px yellow ring for focus.

Set display type in Montserrat 700/800 with 0.02em tracking, Title Case or UPPERCASE for short labels, and body in Montserrat 400/500 at 16–18px/1.6; IBM Plex Mono is reserved for catalogue data — plate numbers, dimensions, dates, durations.

Motion is contemplative: 240–900ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1) fades and 4–8px drifts, plus one slow 28–40s drift loop on a single background arc group; a painting breathes, it does not bounce, spin, or fly in.

Treat color as sound: red is brass and percussive (primary action, emphasis), yellow is high brass and trumpet (highlight, warning), blue is deep string and organ (links, focus, structure), green is the quiet middle voice (success) — and never more than three voices sounding at once in one component.

Stay evocation-only: no reproduction, trace, crop, or scan of any Kandinsky painting, no museum wall text copied verbatim, and no title used as decoration — the style lives in palette, motif, and composition.

componentRecipes.panel: background: #fdfaf3; border: 3px solid #111111; border-radius: 0; padding: 32px; color: #111111; box-shadow: 3px 3px 0 #111111; — the panel's top-right corner may hold one 48px motif cluster (a yellow circle at 60% opacity with a blue quarter-arc crossing it) pinned with position: absolute and overflow: hidden, never overlapping text; headings inside are Montserrat 700 28px with 0.02em tracking, and a 12px #d62828 bar sits above the first line as a scored accent; below 640px drop the hard shadow and the motif, keep the 3px stroke.
componentRecipes.button: font: 700 15px/1 'Montserrat', 'Archivo', system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 16px 32px; border-radius: 0; background: #d62828; color: #fafafa; border: 3px solid #111111; box-shadow: 3px 3px 0 #111111; transition: transform 240ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1), box-shadow 240ms cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1), background-color 240ms linear; :hover { transform: translate(-1px, -1px); box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #111111; } :active { transform: translate(3px, 3px); box-shadow: 0 0 0 #111111; } :focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #1d4ed8; outline-offset: 3px; } — secondary: background #fdfaf3, color #111111, with a 3px #1d4ed8 bar on the left edge; disabled: background #f7f2e8, color #6f6a60, border-color #6f6a60, shadow none, no transform.
componentRecipes.input: font: 15px/1.6 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; color: #111111; background: #fafafa; border: 3px solid #111111; border-radius: 0; padding: 12px 16px; box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0 #1d4ed8; caret-color: #d62828; :placeholder { color: #6f6a60; font: 400 16px 'Montserrat', system-ui, sans-serif; } :focus { background: #fdfaf3; outline: 3px solid #1d4ed8; outline-offset: 2px; } — invalid: border-color #a81f1f, a small red #d62828 circle with a 3px ink stroke beside the field, and a Montserrat 15px sentence below in #a81f1f ('This line cannot be read yet.') so the state never depends on color alone.
componentRecipes.statusbar: height: 56px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 32px; padding: 0 32px; background: #f7f2e8; border-top: 3px solid #111111; border-radius: 0; font: 13px/1.4 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: #111111; left side lists scored events, each prefixed by a 9px outline circle — #2a7d4f passing, #f4b400 pending, #a81f1f failing, #6f6a60 idle; right side holds a mono plate number ('№ 013') and the single primary button; the live event fades between 0.6 and 1 opacity over 900ms instead of blinking.
componentRecipes.menu: vertical catalogue, no bullets, 8px gap: item { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 16px; padding: 12px 16px; font: 500 17px/1.4 'Montserrat', system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #111111; background: transparent; border: 0; border-left: 3px solid transparent; } selected row fills #f4b400, gains a 3px #111111 left bar, and its small index numeral turns #d62828; hover slides translate(4px, 0) over 240ms with the left bar in #1d4ed8; group headers are Montserrat 700 12px spaced 0.14em in #6f6a60 with a 3px #111111 rule beneath spanning 48px.
componentRecipes.badge: catalogue chip, 1–3 words: display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; height: 28px; padding: 0 12px; background: #fafafa; border: 3px solid #111111; border-radius: 0; font: 600 11px/1 'Montserrat', system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #111111; the leading dot is a 10px circle filled #d62828 / #1d4ed8 / #f4b400 / #2a7d4f by role, struck with the same 3px ink stroke; motion is a 240ms fade on state change, never a pulse.

copywriting.voice: A studio voice — a painter annotating their own canvas in pencil. Quiet, precise, present tense, a little synesthetic: copy names the gesture and the material ('Sketch the outline. Paint the circle yellow. Frame it in black.') and treats the interface as a composition being built rather than a tool being used. Never chatty, never promotional; the reader is a visitor in a studio, not a customer.

case.commands: sentence case imperative ('Sketch a note', 'Frame the plate')

avoid: exclamation marks, urgency timers, and pressure tactics
emoji, drop shadows on text, and gradient buttons
any painting title, museum wall text, or gallery copy reproduced from a real exhibition
calling the style 'synesthesia' as a gimmick or a feature name
sarcasm, apology loops, and deadpan errors ('That was not expected.')
all-caps sentences longer than three words

do: Compose each screen as a picture: one dominant mass, one counterweight, one line travelling between them, with generous empty canvas around the ensemble.
Strike every shape with the same 3px #111111 outline and fill it with one trio color — red, blue, or yellow — so shapes read as painted planes cut from paper, not as tinted UI.
Keep the cream ground (#f7f2e8, cards #fdfaf3) visible; the empty space is the composition, so resist filling the corners with decoration.

Build motifs from primitives: Circles are perfect, arcs are quarter to half segments, triangles are equilateral, lines are horizontal or diagonal at 30°/45° — and each motif must carry meaning (selection, status, sequence) rather than acting as confetti.
Use stamped ink depth (3px 3px 0 #111111) plus angled or overlapping shapes to suggest layering, rather than blur, glow, or transparency stacks.

Set display type in Montserrat 700/800 at 24px and up with 0.02em tracking, body in Montserrat 400/500 at 16–18px/1.6, and IBM Plex Mono only for catalogue data — plate numbers, dimensions, dates, durations.
Move slowly: 240–900ms eased fades and 4–8px drifts, one 28–40s background drift, and no motion that competes with reading.
dont: No reproduction of any Kandinsky painting: no scans, traces, crops, thumbnails, or close reconstructions of specific works — evocation only through palette, motif, and composition.
No radius on rectangles, no pills, no soft cards: the only curves in the system are drawn circles and arcs, and the smallest line weight is 3px ink.
No gradients, glassmorphism, backdrop-blur, or low-opacity overlays as decoration; a plane is one opaque fill inside one ink stroke.
No neon glow, no CRT scanlines, no pixelation, no 8-bit type — those belong to the retro modes, and any of them collapses the fine-art register.
No fourth fill hue in the trio: green exists only as the quiet success voice, and violet, teal, magenta, or pastel fills read as a modern app.
No fast or playful motion: no springs, overshoots, spins, parallax bounces, or confetti — and no more than one drifting element in view at a time.
accessibility: Ink #111111 on cream #f7f2e8 clears 4.5:1 comfortably, but trio red #d62828 (≈4.4:1), blue #1d4ed8 (≈5.6:1 at small sizes reads thin), and yellow #f4b400 on cream do not all pass — use them as fills, arcs, strokes, and dots, and set text inside yellow in ink rather than cream.

Keep every canvas motif decorative but not informative on its own: any meaning carried by a circle's color or position must be repeated in a label, a numeral, or a table row, so nothing lives only in a picture.
Montserrat stays at 16px minimum for body copy with 1.6 line-height; the all-caps tracked labels are limited to two or three words and never at sizes below 11px.
Honor prefers-reduced-motion: stop the slow background drift and the drift-on-hover, and let the 240–900ms fades resolve instantly so the composition holds still like a hung painting.
Keep a visible 3px #1d4ed8 focus ring at 3px offset on every focusable element, and never rely on the trio colors alone to mark a state.
signatureElement: The circles-and-arcs composition: a cluster of overlapping ink-stroked circles, quarter-arcs, and ruled line-segments in red, yellow, and blue drifting slowly across a warm cream ground, as if the canvas were sounding a chord

attribution.name: Wassily Kandinsky (1866–1944) — aesthetic reference, Bauhaus and Der Blaue Reiter abstraction
attribution.note: Composition, motif vocabulary, and the color-as-sound idea are inspired by Kandinsky's abstract work; no painting, title, or museum text is reproduced.

attribution.name: Palette derived by eye (cream #f7f2e8, red #d62828, blue #1d4ed8, yellow #f4b400, ink #111111, white #fafafa) from Bauhaus color theory and Kandinsky's primary-trio writing, not sampled from any canvas file

prose.overview: This mode builds the interface as a painted composition: a warm cream canvas, ink-stroked circles, quarter-arcs, triangles, and ruled lines in red, yellow, and blue, arranged with the pacing of a musical score. Every screen is composed rather than populated — one dominant mass, one counterweight, one travelling line — and the empty cream around the ensemble is treated as material, not as wasted space. Kandinsky's synesthetic premise, color heard as sound, becomes the system's hierarchy: red sounds loudly and leads, blue sounds deep and structures, yellow sounds bright and warns. It should feel like standing in front of a hanging canvas that happens to be interactive, never like a retro screen or a gradient-heavy modern dashboard.
prose.colors: The ground is warm cream #f7f2e8 with cards lifted only one step to #fdfaf3 and pure white #fafafa reserved for input wells and badges; ink #111111 carries every outline and nearly all text, with #6f6a60 for muted annotations. Three colors do the talking: red #d62828 is the primary action and the percussive emphasis, blue #1d4ed8 is structure, links, and focus, yellow #f4b400 is highlight and warning, with a darker #a81f1f for hard failure and a quiet green #2a7d4f for success — a fourth voice used sparingly, because a chord of four equally loud colors stops sounding like a composition. Each hue ships with a light/base/dark triad in trioRamps for hover, press, and shadow-step use, and no fill is ever a gradient, a blend, or an alpha composite.
prose.typography: Montserrat leads as the geometric sans — its circular bowls echo the motif vocabulary — set at 700/800 for headings from 24px up with 0.02em tracking, in Title Case for editorial labels and UPPERCASE only for short tracked captions of two or three words. Body copy drops to Montserrat 400/500 at 16–18px with 1.6 line-height, giving paragraphs the airiness of gallery wall text without copying any. IBM Plex Mono appears only for catalogue data: plate numbers, dimensions, dates, durations, and figure references, where its fixed rhythm makes the metadata feel labelled rather than written. No script, no blackletter, no italic pseudo-handwriting: the type stays as ruled and impersonal as the geometry it sits beside.
prose.layout: Layout follows a composition grid: an 8px base with a 4/8/16/32/64px spacing scale, a 12-column field at 32px gutters, and asymmetric placement that gives the eye a dominant mass at roughly two-thirds left and a counterweight circle or arc small and high at the right. Text blocks stay on the column edges — the geometry is allowed to float, the paragraphs are not — so the interface never trades legibility for painting-like balance. Generous margins (64px at desktop, 32px at tablet, 16px at mobile) keep the cream visible, and every motif group is anchored to a grid intersection so the drift animation returns it to exactly where it began.
prose.elevation: Depth is stamped, never lit: 3px 3px 0 #111111 ink offsets lift cards, buttons, and plates, and pressing an element moves it into its own offset (translate(3px,3px) with the shadow collapsed to 0 0 0) so the interaction reads as a paper plane being laid flat. One soft shadow is permitted, 0 16px 40px rgba(17,17,17,.08), for a single floating plate such as a modal or a dragged catalogue card, and it must never stack with a second soft shadow. Layering is otherwise expressed by overlap — a circle crossing a rectangle's edge, an arc sliding under a line — which is how the composition itself creates depth. There are no glossy highlights, no glass panels, no neon glow, and no alpha stacks used as elevation.
prose.shapes: The vocabulary is Euclid's: perfect circles, quarter and half arcs, equilateral triangles, and single ruled line-segments, all struck with the same 3px #111111 outline so every shape looks drawn onto the canvas rather than filled by a UI kit. Rectangles keep radius 0 — a panel is a ruled plane, and rounding it would soften the geometry that carries the whole style. Circles are the signature and may overlap freely, with a smaller circle nested inside a larger one to imply sound or echo; arcs bracket content like a half-frame; triangles point at whatever the page wants read next. Nothing is hand-wobbled, nothing is sketched with a texture brush: the shapes are drafted, and the only organic element allowed is the cream ground itself.
prose.components: Panels are ruled cream planes (#fdfaf3) with a 3px ink border, 32px padding, and one 48px motif cluster clipped into a corner; a 12px red bar scores the top of the first heading. Buttons are ink-struck red rectangles in tracked uppercase Montserrat that translate into their shadow on press, with a cream secondary carrying a blue left bar so it still reads as a plane rather than a ghost. Inputs are white #fafafa wells in IBM Plex Mono with an inset blue spine, turning to paper fill and a blue outline on focus, and errors add both a red dot and a written sentence. The status bar is a scored strip of mono entries each prefixed by an outline circle in green, yellow, or red, closed by a plate number ('№ 013') and the single primary action; menus are catalogue lists whose selected row fills yellow and gains an ink bar, and badges are square ink-struck chips whose leading dot is the role's voice.
prose.dosDonts: Do compose each screen as a picture with one dominant mass and visible cream, do strike every shape with the same 3px ink outline, do keep color to the trio plus a quiet green, and do let motion drift slowly or not at all. Don't reproduce, trace, or crop any Kandinsky painting or its title, don't round a rectangle or reach for gradients and glass, don't import scanlines or pixel fonts from the retro modes, and don't let motifs become decoration with no meaning to carry.
